terms.comment: Properly a lying together; its usual sense is intercourse (Lewis & Short). To have sex with someone: cum aliquō concumbere (Cic. Fat. 30, Lewis & Short), or coīre.
The plain, decent phrase of Cicero and Columella; venerius is the same word.

terms.register: chiefly in poetry and in Pliny and Columella
evidence: Ter. Eun. 732: sine Cerere et Līberō friget Venus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The goddess’s name used for what she presides over, as a euphemism.
Not in Cicero in this sense (Lewis & Short); its general sense is a coming together.

phrases.latin: Concubitus vērō neque nimis concupīscendus, neque nimis pertimēscendus est.
phrases.english: Sex should be neither too much desired nor too much feared.
